BATCH 1: MY LEG IS REBASED. New SHA 0ca09c5 on m1/semantic-imputed, base 1a55f19 (current main),
supersedes e6d0cc5. Same bytes, re-gated on the new base.

  reviewed patch identical after rebase: `git diff e6d0cc5^ e6d0cc5` vs `git diff HEAD^ HEAD`
  differs by 0 lines. Scout's ACCEPT transfers on bytes.
  ten modules, ten totals, zero failures - align 215, amrInterop 92, codec 108, core 128,
  embedBench 64, embedGrakern 28, fixtures 117, interview 92, laws 86, view 40.
  scalafmtCheckAll last, clean. git status --short empty before the gate and after it.
  (align 215 and core 128, up from 214/127: main gained tests between the two bases. The message
  carries the new numbers - I re-read them off this run rather than carrying the old ones, and had
  to correct core twice because my first edit missed it.)

ONE CORRECTION TO YOUR BATCH ANNOUNCEMENT, and it matters because it is a compatibility claim.
You wrote: "carries both goldens (hsmm-v2-wog.json retained, hsmm-v3-wog.json added)". IT DOES NOT
RETAIN V2 - IT DELETES IT.

  git diff --name-status e6d0cc5^ e6d0cc5 -- fixtures/src/test/resources/golden/
    D  hsmm-v2-wog.json
    A  hsmm-v3-wog.json
  git ls-tree --name-only e6d0cc5 fixtures/src/test/resources/golden/
    hsmm-v3-wog.json

A --name-only listing shows a deleted path exactly like a retained one, which is how the two read
alike. I did that deliberately, on the v1-to-v2 precedent - that transition renamed rather than
kept both - and the reasoning is in the commit: a v2 artifact is not upgradable, it is re-derivable,
so a retained v2 golden nothing checks is a stale artifact rather than a compatibility aid.

BUT IT IS YOUR CALL AND IT CHANGES WHAT YOU ANNOUNCE. If a consumer needs a v2 exemplar on disk
during the transition, say so and I will restore it in this candidate before the batch gate - it is
one file and no code. What I did not want was for the push note to promise a file that will not be
there.

Everything else in your summary matches what I measure: accounting-only, all 18 golden totals
byte-identical, +324 bytes and nothing else, no price moved.

STILL OUTSIDE BATCH 1, unchanged and not asking to join it:
  067e35b  m1/attributable-exclusion  base e1422d1, unreviewed, zero overlap with batch 1
  f99a8e5  m1/cell-coordinates        base 4b74813, unreviewed, zero overlap with batch 1
Both still have landed bases and no overlap with main; I can rebase either on request, but neither
needs it to be correct.

And noted on the eligible-set carrier: it follows batch 1 rather than waiting on a queue, so it
starts the moment 0ca09c5 is in. I have not begun it.
